title: Binary-frame-aware tracing middleware and sampling hint propagation for high-throughput edge paths
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our edge proxies sometimes tunnel RPC frames or proprietary binary envelopes that carry compressed metadata. Several internal services (batching, KV cache, and model routing) require low-overhead extraction of trace context and sampling hints from these binary frames so the serving runtime can make routing and cache-warmup decisions without inflating latency. Current HTTP/GRPC middleware handles text headers nicely, but it fails for: 1) non-HTTP binary frames (e.g., multiplexed websocket binary frames, custom wire protocols for internal model switching), and 2) high-throughput paths where allocations and copies dominate tail latency.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, binary-frame-aware tracing middleware for edge SDKs and server frameworks that: (a) zero-copy peeks header envelopes to extract a compact trace context + sampling hint, (b) supports a "probe" mode where a small fraction of requests are fully instrumented and sampled logs are emitted, (c) attaches deterministic origin stamps for downstream dedup/merge logic used by our request coalescer, and (d) exposes a strict, async-safe API for SDKs (Node, Go, Python) to minimize event-loop/blocking risk.

Non-goals: Full OpenTelemetry replacement, complex baggage replication, or speculative rehydration of full KV cache entries within the middleware. This work only extracts ring-fenced context metadata and hint flags for downstream routing/telemetry.

Design notes and constraints: 
- Header envelope is a fixed prelude of 12 bytes when present: 0x52 0x49 0x44 0x00 (magic), 1 byte version, 1 byte flags, 4 bytes trace_id_prefix (first 32 bits), 2 bytes sampling_hint. The middleware must be resilient if magic or length missing.
- Must support fallbacks: text-header extraction (X-Redwood-Trace / Traceparent) -> binary envelope -> opaque fingerprint heuristic.
- Must avoid heap allocations on hot path in Go / Node native addons; implement zero-copy peeking and stack-buffer parsing for frames < 256 bytes.
- Provide a consistent public SDK method: extractTraceContext(frameBytes) -> [trace_id_prefix, sampling_hint, origin_stamp] or null. The return values are small fixed-size buffers/strings.
- Sampling hints: {0: unknown, 1: eager-sample, 2: probe-sample, 3: never-sample}. Probe-sample instructs runtime to record lightweight metrics and capture a condensed event for downstream quality evaluation.

Implementation plan: 
1) Prototype in Go edge-proxy codepath (edge-proxy v0.41) with zero-copy peek and a fast-path for 12-byte magic. Add unit tests with fuzz cases for partial frames. 
2) Add Node SDK binding that exposes same API. Use napi/native addon to avoid copying for Buffer-backed frames.
3) Add Python C-extension shim for async frameworks (uvloop/asyncio) to avoid GIL bottlenecks in the hot path. If C-extension is not feasible in the timeframe, implement a pure-python fallback with CFFI optimization.
4) Update runtime routing policy to consult sampling_hint when deciding to: (a) route to higher-fidelity models, (b) trigger async cache warmups, (c) emit a lightweight trace sample.
5) Add a probe-mode config flag to enable 0.1% of requests to be marked as probe-sample even when hint absent, to seed quality monitors.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Middleware extracts correct context for 99.999% of synthetic golden traces and gracefully returns null when envelope absent or malformed.
- End-to-end latency regression on the hot path is <1ms P99 for median 8KB frames. Allocation delta on Go hot path < 64 bytes per extraction.
- SDKs (Go, Node) expose stable API and pass cross-language conformance tests.
- Runtime successfully consumes sampling_hint for cache warmup decisions in canary traffic.
- Integration smoke test + perf benchmark run on dedicated CI and results checked into the feature branch.

Docs and links: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Binary+Frame+Tracing+Middleware+Design
- Prototype PR (Go edge-proxy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1426
- Node SDK proposal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Zl_edge_node_trace_proposal
- Runtime routing change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/884

Security and privacy notes: 
- The middleware only reads a 12-byte header and does not log payload content. Sampling decisions must obey tenant privacy settings (disable_probe flag). For Private deployments, ensure we only consult headers within VPC boundary (no cross-tenant forwarding).

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (internal canary): enable on 10% internal edge hosts for 2 weeks, collect probe samples and latency metrics.
- Phase 2 (customer beta): opt-in flag in console to enable sampling hints for specific tenants.
- Phase 3: default enable for internal traffic after 6 weeks if no regressive metrics.
